content: The medication described is used to treat a variety of bacterial infections and belongs to the carbapenem class of antibiotics. It is administered via injection into a muscle or vein, typically every 6 to 8 hours, as directed by a healthcare provider. If you are administering this medication at home, it is essential to learn proper preparation and usage techniques from your healthcare professional. Before use, inspect the medication for particles or discoloration, and do not use it if either is present. For optimal effectiveness, take the medication at evenly spaced intervals and complete the full prescribed course, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects may include swelling, redness, pain, or soreness at the injection site. Rarely, it may cause stomach upset, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. However, in rare cases, it may lead to a severe intestinal condition caused by the bacteria Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile), which can occur during treatment or weeks to months after stopping the medication. Prolonged or repeated use may result in oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. Before using this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to any of its ingredients, other carbapenems (e.g., meropenem), penicillins, cephalosporins, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Additionally, this medication may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine). During pregnancy, it should only be used when clearly necessary, and it is known to pass into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how this medication works or increase the risk of serious side effects. It is important to keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests, such as urine glucose tests, potentially causing false results. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition and should not be used for other purposes. While using this medication, your doctor may order lab tests, such as complete blood counts and kidney or liver function tests, to monitor your progress. If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. For storage, consult the product instructions or your pharmacist for specific details. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
